reviews.body:
Good fix. `AudioOutput` now has the same url / data-URL handling as the image and video outputs, and resolving the bytes before opening the file means a failed download or decode can no longer truncate an existing file. The "failed save keeps existing file" test pins that down nicely, and so does the one checking that `data:` URLs never reach `requests`.

A few thoughts:

The `try` around `import requests` also wraps the `requests.get(...)` call. Only `ImportError` is caught, so it works, but narrowing the `try` to just the import makes it clearer that network errors are meant to propagate.

Resolving first fixes the decode/download case, but `open(path, "wb")` still truncates before writing. If the write itself fails partway (disk full, permission change), the old file is gone. Writing to a temp file in the same directory and `os.replace()`-ing it would make `save()` fully atomic, if that matters here.

Since this mirrors the `VideoOutput` logic, pulling `_resolve_bytes` into one shared helper would stop the outputs from drifting apart again (which seems to be how audio fell behind in the first place).

Thanks for the review. I narrowed the `try` in `AudioOutput._resolve_bytes` to just the `requests` import, so it's clear that network and HTTP errors are meant to propagate (no behaviour change).

I've left the other two out of this PR. A temp file plus `os.replace()` would make `save()` atomic, and a shared `_resolve_bytes` helper would keep the outputs from drifting, but both are best applied across all the output classes rather than only audio. I can open a follow-up for that if the maintainers want it.
